clue.text: Unable to leave home-or travelling there?

definitions.meaning: someone confined indoors by illness or age cannot get out of the house
read as 'bound for the house', i.e. heading towards the home just mentioned

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is stuck indoors or merely on their way back.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition leans on 'home' in the first: something bound for a house is travelling there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings work: confined indoors, or literally heading (bound) for the house.

clue.text: Henry has stirred the reheated dish

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance

indicators.note: stirred means the letters of has are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook named Henry stirs a warmed-up meal.
explanation.walkthrough: The page prints 'there heated'; the word break belongs after 'the', making 'the reheated dish' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hash is a dish of chopped leftover meat cooked up again, the classic reheated meal.

clue.text: The bone used in some beautiful Namibian carvings

indicators.note: the letters sit inside part of the run beautiful Namibian, spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A bone is used by craftsmen in Namibian carvings.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two forearm bones, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: I need another hundred to make it like paradise

indicators.note: another signals making a different arrangement of the letters given

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone needs yet another hundred pounds to make life heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' rearranges INEED plus C into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Garden of Eden is the biblical paradise, so the adjective describes anything paradisal.

clue.text: Humble subscription by a deferential menial

definitions.meaning: a subscription here is the formal sign-off at the foot of an old-fashioned letter
a servant who does as told and bows to the master

explanation.surface: A formal letter is signed off modestly by a bowing servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subscription' means the words written under a letter, not a magazine order.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Your obedient servant' was the formal letter closing; literally it also describes a dutiful domestic.

clue.text: Being annoyed, informed the police

definitions.meaning: a nark is a police informer, so to nark is to grass someone up

explanation.surface: Someone irritated by events goes and tells the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: irritated, and having acted as a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'narked' means irritated; 'to nark' is to act as a police informer.

clue.text: Medal struck before dinner

definitions.meaning: British slang for a medal or decoration
a metal disc hit to summon a household to the table

explanation.surface: A medal is pinned on just before a formal meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a decoration, and the disc beaten in country houses to call people to eat.

clue.text: Rook accomplished attack

parts.note: a task accomplished is over, finished
a charge is an attacking rush

explanation.surface: A chess rook completes an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' is not the chess piece or the bird but the verb meaning to swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to fleece someone, charging them far too much.

clue.text: Present to little Ken on Sunday

definitions.text: Present to little Ken on Sunday

parts.note: a present is a gift
taken as written
Ken is the short form of Kenneth

explanation.surface: Someone gives young Ken something on Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and a picture of the vouchers being given.
explanation.definitionFit: Vouchers exchangeable in shops are a common present, so the whole scene describes them.

clue.text: Viewers should hold on to catch "The Poets"

indicators.note: viewers holding something means it goes inside the word for them

parts.note: seers are people who see, viewers
to net a fish is to catch it

explanation.surface: Television viewers are told to tune in for a programme about poets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should hold' sounds like a TV announcer's instruction, but 'hold' is the container signal and 'should' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers of fourteen-line verses are poets of a particular kind.

clue.text: Unable to hear the fade out

indicators.note: out signals the letters of fade are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone cannot hear the sound as it fades away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges FADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the sense of hearing is the plain meaning.

clue.text: Target-round that is any colour?

parts.note: an object is a target or aim
a ball is a round thing

explanation.surface: A round target that can be painted in any colour.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the ball a player aims at with the cue ball may be any of the coloured balls.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker or pool the ball aimed at may be red, black or any coloured one.

clue.text: Parade for the said period

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: said signals a word that sounds like a period

parts.note: a session is a period of activity

explanation.surface: A parade staged for a particular time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives CESSION, a word for surrender that sounds like SESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession is an orderly parade or march.

clue.text: Is invited to define what the caller did

annotationWithheld.why: Is invited to define what the caller did: VISITED appears to read 'in-vited' as IS inside VITED, splitting the word invited, and no parse with whole clue words gives the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: Is invited to define what the caller did

clue.text: Left act with Dave performing

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters act out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Dave leaves the stage after his act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges ACT and DAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacated means moved out of, so having left a place.

clue.text: Meals eaten by those who eat meals around the north

indicators.note: diners around something means it sits inside the word

parts.note: diners are people eating meals
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: Meals are consumed by northern diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside DINERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Evening or main repasts are the everyday sense.

clue.text: Wine available to Arabs wandering about

indicators.note: wandering means the letters of Arabs stray into a new order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Wine is on offer to nomadic Arabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available to' is padding that joins definition and wordplay; Barsac is a commune in the Sauternes area.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Made baby's bed in Berkshire

parts.note: did means made or performed
a cot is a child's bed with high sides

explanation.surface: Someone made up a baby's bed in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Didcot is a railway town that was in the county of Berkshire until the 1974 boundary changes moved it to Oxfordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: A town that belonged to that county when this puzzle was set.

clue.text: It is in print, for crying out loud!

definitions.text: It is in print, for crying out loud!

parts.words: It is in print, for crying out loud
parts.note: the punctuation used in writing to show a shout or outburst, such as the one ending this clue

explanation.surface: An exasperated outburst about something being published.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for crying out loud' looks like an exclamation of annoyance but describes the punctuation's job.
explanation.definitionFit: The symbol written to show a cry or emphatic remark in printed text.

clue.text: Pretty useless hanger-on?

parts.note: a decorative bunch of threads that dangles from curtains or cushions and serves no purpose

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a parasitic hanger-on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty useless' sounds like 'quite useless' but means ornamental and functionless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental bunch of threads that simply hangs from fabric, decorative yet pointless.

clue.text: An article to be followed

definitions.meaning: a person at the front whom others go after

explanation.surface: Instructions say a set of rules must be obeyed.
explanation.walkthrough: A leading article is a newspaper editorial; a person at the head is followed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both an editorial column in a paper and the person heading a group.

clue.text: Spanish place where drunken Nora hid silver

indicators.note: Nora hiding something means it goes inside her rearranged name
drunken signals the letters of Nora reel into a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: In Spain a tipsy woman named Nora stashes her silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where' joins the definition to the wordplay; Nora's drunkenness is the anagram signal, not a story detail.
explanation.definitionFit: A historic kingdom and modern region of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Remarks that are made incidentally

parts.note: comments dropped in passing, off the main subject, or murmured on stage for the audience only

explanation.surface: A description of offhand comments.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing comments that digress from the main topic.

clue.text: Cast down drain

definitions.meaning: to make someone low in spirits
to sap someone's energy and spirit, leaving them dejected

explanation.surface: Something is thrown into a gutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drain' is the verb meaning sap or exhaust, not the gutter it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispirit someone is to cast them down, and wearing tasks sap or drain them.

clue.text: A fish month for Jews

parts.note: the bib is a small fish of the cod family, also called pout

explanation.surface: A fish eaten during a Jewish month.
explanation.walkthrough: BIB is a cod-like fish found in European waters.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical name of the first month of the Hebrew calendar, later called Nisan.

clue.text: Fellow recurrently dined on Greek cheese

indicators.note: recurrently, read as running back, means the word for dined is turned round

parts.note: ate means dined

explanation.surface: A man repeatedly eats Greek cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrently' reverses ATE to give ETA, under F.
explanation.definitionFit: A white brined cheese made from sheep's milk in Greece.

clue.text: Does this work cause worry?

definitions.meaning: placed before work, the word names decorative cut-out woodwork

explanation.surface: A nervous question about whether a gadget will function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this work' is fretwork, ornamental woodwork, rather than the 'will it function' of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Fretwork is ornamental woodcarving; to vex someone is to make them anxious.

clue.text: Drawback admitted by rebel leader to humorous poet

indicators.note: something admitted by a word is let inside it
rebel signals the letters of leader revolt into a new order

parts.note: drawback split as draw plus back: draw read backwards gives these letters

explanation.surface: A rebel chief concedes a drawback to a comic poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawback' looks like one noun meaning disadvantage, but it splits into 'Draw' plus the reversal signal 'back'; 'rebel' shuffles the six letters of 'leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks, such as 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat'.

clue.text: Come down to earth

definitions.meaning: to touch down after a flight

explanation.surface: An instruction to stop daydreaming and be realistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface idiom 'come down to earth' splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To touch down, and the solid ground as opposed to sea.

clue.text: Church member taking professional exam sitting by a social worker

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a test is an exam
an ant is a social insect, and workers are its labouring caste

explanation.surface: A churchgoer takes a professional exam next to a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a council employee but an insect from a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of a Western church that broke from Rome at the Reformation.
